podcast.title: Dispute with Damon Albarn (Post-2010)
podcast.body: Following "The Fall" album, Jamie Hewlett and Damon Albarn had a falling out for about four years. Hewlett reportedly felt that the music was becoming too prominent, overshadowing his comic creations, leading to his dissatisfaction. "The Jamie, the music was getting bigger while his comic creations were taking more of a back seat. Didn't like that very much."

podcast.title: Aging of Characters
podcast.body: Hewlett became "a little bored with the characters" and decided to age them up, most notably Noodle, who transitioned from a 10-year-old girl to a 17-year-old teen. "Jamie had grown a little bored with the characters, so he decided to age them up a bit."

podcast.title: Album Artwork
podcast.body: Hewlett's "Tank Girl" work led to commissions for album artwork, including the EP "You Got It!" by the British group Senseless Things, featuring a distinctive drawing of an alien. "He and his buddy, Alan Martin, had their own strip called Tank Girl."

podcast.title: Diverse Creative Projects
podcast.body: Beyond comics, Hewlett designed nightclub decor, opened a clothing store, wrote for a computer magazine, and created a comic strip about a gay Buddhist kung fu cop. "He also designed the decor for a nightclub. He opened a clothing store. He wrote for a computer magazine."

podcast.title: Early Career
podcast.body: In the late 1980s, Jamie Hewlett worked for the British magazine "Deadline," known for comic strips and drawings. He co-created the strip "Tank Girl" with Alan Martin. "By the late 1980s, he was working for a British magazine called Deadline, which featured comic strips and drawings by a variety of English artists."

podcast.title: Inspiration for Gorillaz Characters
podcast.body: While sharing a London flat with Damon Albarn in 1997, Hewlett, inspired by MTV's perceived lack of substance, created the four fictional members of Gorillaz: 2D, Murdoc, Noodle, and Russell. "Jamie came up with 2D, Murdoch, Noodle and Russell."

podcast.title: Pulp's "Common People" Comic Strip
podcast.body: In 1995, Hewlett illustrated a comic strip based on the story of Pulp's song "Common People," which was included with the French version of the single and an Australian box set. This connection highlights his acquaintanceship with Pulp's Jarvis Cocker. "He also illustrated a comic strip in 1995 that was based entirely on the story told in this song by Pulp."

podcast.title: Tank Girl Movie
podcast.body: His comic strip "Tank Girl" was optioned for a movie, which was made in 1995. Prior to this, Steven Spielberg had expressed interest in working with Hewlett. "It was option for a movie that was made in 1995."

xref.title: Creation and Concept
xref.body: Formed by Damon Albarn and Jamie Hewlett in 1997, the band originated from their observations of MTV artists' perceived vacuity and lack of substance. The idea was to create a "fake band" with fictional characters to comment on contemporary music. "Bloody hell, somebody said, we should just form a fake band. You make some music, all draw the characters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Failed Movie Project
xref.body: Jamie Hewlett worked on a script for a Gorillaz movie during the "Demon Days" period, with interest from Harvey Weinstein and Terry Gilliam, and a working title "Bananas" (spelled with a Z). However, the movie never materialized, though ideas were integrated into the album, songs, and music videos, with fans eventually receiving an online documentary. "The movie never happened, but ideas were integrated into the album, the songs, and the music videos."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inspiration for Gorillaz
xref.body: While sharing a London flat with Jamie Hewlett in 1997, Damon Albarn watched MTV and was struck by the perceived vacuity and lack of substance in many contemporary artists, leading to the idea of forming a "fake band." "The TV was on MTV a lot and both of them were fascinated by how vacuous so many of the artists were, how empty the music was, how little substance there seemed to be."

xref.title: Introduction to Jamie Hewlett

xref.title: Suspected Identities
xref.body: Some speculate that Banksy might be 3D (Robert Del Naja) from the group Massive Attack, or Jamie Hewlett, who collaborates with Damon Albarn on Gorillaz. Another theory suggests he is Robin Gunningham, an artist from Bristol who once called himself Robin Banks, potentially evolving into Banksy. "Although some suspect that he might be 3D, otherwise known as Robert Naja in the group Massive Attack. Or maybe Banksy is actually Jamie Hewitt, the guy who works with Damon Albard and Gorillas. Or it might be a guy named Robin Gunningham, an artist from Bristol who started calling himself Robin Banks, which may have eventually become Banksy."

xref.title: Virtual Band Conception
xref.body: Gorillaz were conceived in 1998 as a virtual band, a creative project by Blur's Damon Albarn and cartoonist Jamie Hewlett. "Gorillas, the virtual band created by Blur's Damon Albarn and cartoonist Jamie Hewlett. They were conceived in 1998."
